title: Investigate why the merge phase leaves a staged revert of the just-merged code in the main repo index and working tree
userDescription:
Investigate why the merge phase leaves a staged REVERT of the just-merged code in the main repo working tree and index. This has happened more than once. Do not fix yet - the deliverable is a diagnosis naming the exact line that writes the index and the exact line that rewrites the working tree.

OBSERVED RUN: runId msjg9ajc-tx9rtcb8kmn, 2026-08-07, task 111, base branch new-usage-graph pinned at 8e431bb47fa271b45dc85dec4edbc4f2086b0283.

ORDER OF EVENTS, each verified in this session rather than inferred:

1. 21:21:20Z prepareTasks.ts ran, printed "Reset branch task-group-1", pinned baseOid 8e431bb. Git status captured at session start showed plans/brief-112.md and plans/task-112-plan.md as UNTRACKED with the ?? marker, and .taskTools/tasks.json as modified-but-unstaged. Record this - it matters at step 7.
2. Plan and verify workflows wrote plans/task-111-plan.md. Codex reviewed twice.
3. Implement workflow committed cd6e064 on branch task-group-1 in the worktree at taskTools-wt/taskTools/group-1.
4. A follow-up commit d0931c8 in the same worktree removed two dead type imports from scripts/mergePipeline.ts. Test workflow reported green.
5. Worktree inspected directly - HEAD d0931c8, clean except untracked plans/p.md, base still 8e431bb, no drift. Backup branch task-111-backup force-created at d0931c8.
6. .taskTools/run-steps.json written, then the merge ran as node scripts/runMergePhase.ts. It printed status merged, publicationTargets targetOid 08780dc1980b2a34f99b1888b261d51c6d89f956, recordedBaseOid 8e431bb, approval.recordedAt 2026-08-07T21:45:05.234Z, conflicts empty, abortReason null.
7. Immediately after the merge, git status --porcelain in the MAIN repo showed scripts/mergePipeline.ts, scripts/operationBranches.ts, scripts/prepareTasks.ts, scripts/runMergePhase.ts and tests/runMergePhase.test.ts all with the staged marker, AND plans/brief-112.md plus plans/task-112-plan.md with the staged-add marker. Those last two were UNTRACKED at step 1 and nothing in this session staged them, so the merge phase itself staged files it did not own.
8. git diff --cached proved the DIRECTION of the staged change was a revert - the index held the PRE-task-111 content. It removed the buildOperationPushOccurrences import and its call from prepareTasks.ts, removed resolveMergeVerdict from runMergePhase.ts, and reverted the new imports in tests/runMergePhase.test.ts. The working tree files on disk matched the index, also lacking the fix. Meanwhile git show HEAD on each of the five files confirmed the merged commit 08780dc DID contain the fix. So HEAD was correct while index and worktree were both rolled back.
9. Recovery that worked - git checkout HEAD -- on the five files restored index and worktree together. Typecheck clean and the 9 tests in tests/runMergePhase.test.ts passed afterwards.

CRITICAL AMBIGUITY THE INVESTIGATION MUST RESOLVE FIRST. Between the merge and step 7 a full npx tsc --noEmit plus npm test run reported 1150 pass and 0 fail, which was read at the time as proof the worktree was still correct. That reading is probably WRONG. The previous session on this branch reported 1161 tests with 1 failure. The count dropped by 11. A reverted tests/runMergePhase.test.ts holds 7 tests instead of 9, and a reverted tree would drop other tests too, so a smaller all-passing suite is exactly what a reverted tree produces. Determine whether the revert landed during the merge subprocess or after it. The test-count delta is the strongest available evidence and points at during. Do not trust a green suite as proof the tree is intact - compare test COUNTS against the previous run.

LEADS ALREADY GATHERED, to save the next agent the grep:
- scripts/runFinalizer.ts lines 52-61, function stageChange, runs git add on the REAL index of repoRoot with no GIT_INDEX_FILE isolation. This is the only code path found that stages arbitrary paths into the main repo index. It stages whatever change.path lists, so if the working tree holds older content at that moment, git add snapshots the OLD bytes into the index. Prime suspect for the staging half.
- scripts/mergeTaskWorktrees.ts line 179 runs git checkout sourceBranch in repoRoot, and line 216 does the same in mainSubmodulePath. A branch checkout rewrites the working tree. Prime suspect for the disk-revert half. Line 204 runs git add on conflicted paths, but this run had zero conflicts so that path did not execute.
- scripts/recoveryRefs.ts line 29 runs git add -A but appears to pass a GIT_INDEX_FILE env - verify that the env is actually applied before ruling it out.
- ALREADY RULED OUT - scripts/repositoryIntegration.ts lines 39-60, substituteGitlink, correctly isolates its read-tree and update-index behind a scratch GIT_INDEX_FILE and removes it in a finally block. Do not spend time here.
- Only scripts/recoveryRefs.ts and scripts/repositoryIntegration.ts use GIT_INDEX_FILE at all, so every other git add, checkout, read-tree or update-index in scripts/ touches the real index or the real worktree.

WHY IT MATTERS: if the staged revert is committed by the user or by a later automated step, the merged task is silently undone while tasks.json already records it as completed with the commit hash. Also note the merge phase archived task 111 into completedTasks.json with commitHashes 08780dc but wrote no closureNote, which is a separate small gap in the same post-merge code path and worth confirming during recon.

Files to investigate: scripts/runFinalizer.ts, scripts/mergeTaskWorktrees.ts, scripts/mergePipeline.ts, scripts/runMergePhase.ts, scripts/recoveryRefs.ts, scripts/runConsolidation.ts, scripts/repositoryIntegration.ts

Suggested verification: run a full tackle-tasks cycle on a scratch task in a temp clone, snapshot git status --porcelain and git diff --cached before and after the merge subprocess, and assert the index contains no entry whose content is older than HEAD.

Difficulty around 6.
description:
Diagnosis-only task: name the exact line that writes the main repo index and the exact line that rewrites the main repo working tree after a successful merge. Do not ship a fix under this task.

Recon already performed while filing this task, so the next agent does not repeat it:

- scripts/runFinalizer.ts lines 52-61 define stageChange, which calls git(repoRoot, "add", "--", change.path) (and the two-path form for renames) against the REAL index of repoRoot. Its local git() helper at lines 48-50 is a plain execFileSync with no GIT_INDEX_FILE in env. Because git add snapshots whatever bytes are on disk at call time, a working tree already rolled back would be committed into the index as a revert. Prime suspect for the staging half of the symptom.
- scripts/mergeTaskWorktrees.ts line 179 calls git(repoRoot, "checkout", sourceBranch) in the main checkout, and line 216 does the same against mainSubmodulePath. A branch checkout rewrites tracked files on disk. Prime suspect for the disk-revert half. Line 204 (git add of conflictedPaths) did not execute in the observed run because conflicts was empty.
- scripts/recoveryRefs.ts line 29 runs git add -A with an env argument that appears to carry GIT_INDEX_FILE; confirm the env is actually threaded through before ruling it out.
- RULED OUT: scripts/repositoryIntegration.ts substituteGitlink, lines 34-61. It allocates a scratch index path under tmpdir(), passes it as GIT_INDEX_FILE to both read-tree (line 42) and update-index (lines 43-47), and rmSync's it in a finally block (lines 58-60). Correctly isolated. Do not spend time here.
- A repo-wide grep showed only scripts/recoveryRefs.ts and scripts/repositoryIntegration.ts reference GIT_INDEX_FILE at all, so every other git add / checkout / read-tree / update-index under scripts/ mutates the real index or the real worktree.

Evidence from the observed run (runId msjg9ajc-tx9rtcb8kmn, task 111, base new-usage-graph at 8e431bb47fa271b45dc85dec4edbc4f2086b0283):

- Merge printed status merged, publicationTargets targetOid 08780dc1980b2a34f99b1888b261d51c6d89f956, recordedBaseOid 8e431bb, conflicts empty, abortReason null, approval.recordedAt 2026-08-07T21:45:05.234Z.

SECOND OCCURRENCE, task 112, runId msjm112r-taskonetwelve, base new-usage-graph at 54a60c40fe9b1af6b62e5d4ca950ff5eeb1345b0, merged as 7c28efbc48e2262b947beeb6a6d71c20837ea14c. Same symptom, and it supplies a leading hypothesis: the staged revert is caused by the merge phase moving the ref without updating the working tree. Under that explanation nothing actively writes a revert - the branch ref advances to the new merge commit while the index and the on-disk files are simply left at the pre-merge base, and git diff --cached then renders that staleness as deletions of everything the merge added.

Evidence from the task 112 run that discriminates this hypothesis from an active-revert one, all checked rather than inferred:
- git diff 54a60c4 -- scripts/ tests/ was EMPTY, and git diff --cached 54a60c4 -- scripts/ tests/ was EMPTY. Index and working tree were byte-identical to the pre-merge base, not to some third intermediate state. An active revert written by stageChange from stale disk bytes would be expected to reproduce the base content too, so this does not by itself rule out runFinalizer.ts, but it does confirm the reverted state is exactly the base tree with nothing else mixed in.
- git diff --cached against HEAD showed 42 insertions and 482 deletions across 6 files, with tests/mergePipeline.test.ts staged as a deletion (D). That file is new in the merged commit, so its absence from index and disk is consistent with the tree never having been advanced.
- HEAD was correct throughout: git show HEAD:scripts/runMergePhase.ts contained archiveIfMerged twice, while the on-disk copy contained it zero times and tests/mergePipeline.test.ts did not exist on disk.
- Recovery: git checkout HEAD -- scripts/ tests/ restored index and worktree together, after which typecheck was clean and the suite was 1165 pass / 0 fail.

title: tackle-tasks: programmatic owned-files fence check after the implement commit
userDescription:
## Goal

**Chain goal (tasks 137-138):** The same `task.workflow.js` implements the approved plan inside the task's worktree, runs the task's own tests, commits, and then proves in code that the commit touched only the files the task owns.

**This task is done when all of these are true:**

- After the implement agent commits, the workflow runs `git -C <worktree> diff --name-only <base>..HEAD` in plain code — not as an instruction to an agent.
- Every path in that output is compared against the task's own `files` list.
- Any path outside that list is recorded as a fence violation and carried forward to the approval gate.
- A fence violation NEVER undoes work. The check does not revert, reset, checkout, stash, amend, or re-run the implementer. The commit and the worktree are left exactly as the implementer left them.
- The fence is a check that can actually report a violation, replacing today's situation where it exists only as a sentence in the worker's prompt (implement.workflow.js:84) and nothing verifies it.
- Deciding what to do about a violation belongs to the approval gate (task 141), not to this check.
- `plans/task-<N>-implementation-notes.md` is exempt from the fence check — it is expected output of the implement stage, not a violation.

title: tackle-tasks: rebase-test stage — merge-conflict agent fed from collectConflictedRebasePaths
userDescription:
## Goal

**Chain goal (tasks 145-146):** The rebase-test stage of `task.workflow.js` turns a rebased task branch into a mergeable, green branch: rebase conflicts go to a merge agent handed the exact conflicted paths, and a layer whose tests fail gets a fix agent and a bounded retry. A task reaches the merge stage only with every layer green.

**This task is done when all of these are true:**

- The rebase-test stage exists in `task.workflow.js` and drives the per-layer rebase walk built in tasks 142 and 143.
- When a rebase leaves conflicts, the merge agent is HANDED the conflicted paths from `collectConflictedRebasePaths` (in `scripts/mergeTaskWorktrees.ts` — find it by name, its line numbers have drifted), so it never has to search the repository to discover which files conflicted. Handing over the paths is a starting point, not a scope limit.
- The conflict is handed over LIVE: `rebaseGroupOntoSource` gains a mode that returns the conflicted paths WITHOUT aborting, so the agent edits real conflict markers in the working tree and the caller then drives `git rebase --continue` or `--abort`. Today it aborts first, leaving the agent only filenames and a clean tree.
- READ SCOPE: the agent may read anything, anywhere in the tree — callers, callees, tests, other layers.
- EDIT SCOPE: the agent may edit any file in any layer. Resolving a conflict often means updating a call site, and a call site can live in a different repository.
- Every edit the agent makes in a layer is COMMITTED to that layer's `task-N` branch before the walk continues. It never leaves loose working-tree changes: `git rebase` requires a clean tree, so an uncommitted edit in a not-yet-rebased layer would break that layer's rebase, while a committed one is simply carried by it.
- ONE RULE GOVERNS ALL REBASE TESTING: when a submodule changes, every layer is tested. No per-layer green flags, no dirty marking, no staleness bookkeeping — a submodule change means the whole tree is re-tested before the task may merge, and a layer's suite running more than once is expected.
- Files edited outside the handed-over conflicted paths are REPORTED, not blocked — same rule as the task 138 fence: recorded and surfaced, never undone.
- Whatever remains useful in `merge.workflow.js`'s conflict-fixing prompt is folded into this stage.
- Deleting `merge.workflow.js` is NOT part of this task — the old workflow files are removed at the end of the chain.
- The green gate and its fix loop are task 146, not this task.

description:
Split of task 130, step 2 of 4. Wires the `merge` stage of skills/tackle-tasks/task.workflow.js to the per-task merge primitive built by tasks 142, 143 and 144.

TWO KINDS OF MERGE, ONE ORDERED LAP. Every task's lap performs both, in this order: (a) each submodule's `task-N` branch merges into that submodule's own source branch, deepest layer first, and each containing repository's gitlink is resolved to the just-merged commit, propagating up the chain; then (b) the parent's `task-N` branch merges into the parent's source branch. These are genuinely different functions — mergeSubmoduleBranchIntoRepo needs an explicit `git fetch` because a submodule inside a worktree is a separate checkout, while mergeGroupBranchIntoRepo does not, since a parent worktree shares the root repo's object store. They are not one function parameterised by layer. Both live in scripts/mergeTaskWorktrees.ts; find them by name, not by line number.

For one task, after cleanup (task 150) and after the rebase-test stage reports every layer green (tasks 145-146): perform that ordered lap through the primitive. That is where this stage ends.

Do not reimplement the submodule-before-parent ordering here. It already lives in the primitive; a second copy in the workflow is exactly how the two drift apart. If the primitive turns out to miss a layer, fix it in scripts/mergeTaskWorktrees.ts, which is in this task's files for that purpose.

The parent's source branch must never, at any moment, point at a commit that exists only on a task branch. A reader who fetches between the submodule merge and the parent merge must still get a resolvable tree.

This stage is launched by the merge scheduling queue (task 147); it is not called by the queue's own code. The queue schedules, the stage merges.

SCOPE BOUNDARY — read this before reviewing a plan for this task as incomplete.

This task merges. It does NOT close the task and it does NOT remove the worktree, and a plan that omits both is correct, not deficient.

Closing is task 152 ("call closeTasks directly, gated on the verified merged commit hash"), which shares skills/tackle-tasks/task.workflow.js with this task and runs immediately after this stage. A reviewer looking at a stage that merges but never marks the task done in tasks.json is looking at a deliberate boundary, not an omission.

removeWorktreeAndBranch is likewise NOT called here. plans/task-86-spec.md item 6 fixes its position: "On success: delete plan + brief (keeping the implementation notes), merge, run `scripts/closeTasks.ts` directly (no subagent), and `removeWorktreeAndBranch` **last**, so any earlier failure leaves the worktree for inspection." Task 152 places that call, after its verified close succeeds. Calling it here would destroy the worktree before the close is verified, and task 153 requires that a failed close leave the worktree and its task-N branch intact for a human to inspect. The existing `runMergeCli` convention of removing the worktree the moment a merge reports success is the pattern being replaced, not the pattern to copy.

FAILURE CONTRACT. A failure at any layer returns a discrete outcome distinguishing a submodule-layer failure from a parent-layer failure, carried out of the attempt for task 149 to report. Submodule source branches that already merged before the failure are NOT rolled back — see task 153.

title: tackle-tasks: call closeTasks directly, gated on the verified merged commit hash
userDescription:
## Goal

**Chain goal (tasks 150-153):** A task that clears the merge queue is completely finished — plan and brief deleted in the same commit, implementation notes committed, branches merged submodule-first, worktree removed, and the task archived against the verified merge commit hash — while a task that fails any step of its lap lands nothing further.

**This task is done when all of these are true:**

- `scripts/closeTasks.ts` is called DIRECTLY as plain code — no subagent, unlike the close-tasks skill's current path.
- Closing is gated on the merge having actually succeeded, verified against the merged commit hash — not on the pipeline having reached this step.
- closeTasks records that actual merged commit hash.
- WRITES TO tasks.json USE THIS EXACT SEQUENCE, with `node:fs` and `node:crypto` only — no new dependency:
    1. `readFileSync(tasksPath)` → bytes
    2. `createHash("sha256").update(bytes).digest("hex")` → hashBefore
    3. apply the archive to the parsed value
    4. `writeFileSync(tmpPath, next)` where tmpPath is in the SAME directory (`.taskTools/`), e.g. `.taskTools/.tasks.json.<pid>.tmp`
    5. re-read and re-hash `tasksPath`; if it no longer equals hashBefore, `unlinkSync(tmpPath)` and go back to step 1, bounded retries
    6. otherwise `renameSync(tmpPath, tasksPath)`
- `renameSync` within one filesystem is atomic on POSIX, so no reader ever sees a half-written tasks.json, and a crashed run leaves only a temp file, never a lock that wedges the next run.
- THE SAME hash-guarded sequence protects `.taskTools/completedTasks.json`, not only tasks.json. Write completedTasks.json FIRST, then remove from tasks.json, so a crash between the two leaves the record in both files (visible, repairable) rather than in neither (lost).
- `removeWorktreeAndBranch` runs LAST, after the verified close. If only that final call fails, the task is still merged and still closed: report a cleanup warning naming the worktree and branch, do not unwind the merge and do not reopen the task.
- A task whose merge was skipped or blocked, or which hit the 2-lap ceiling, is still present in tasks.json when the run ends.
- If the merge SUCCEEDED but every retry failed, the merge is NOT unwound: the task stays open, the worktree is NOT removed, and the run reports MERGED BUT NOT CLOSED.
- TEST: on success, closeTasks records the actual merged commit hash.
- TEST: a task that was skipped or blocked is still open when the run ends.
- SCOPE OF THE GUARANTEE, NARROWED 2026-08-09 BY USER DECISION. The sequence above cannot make the whole read-to-rename span safe: a writer that lands between the step 5 re-hash and the step 6 renameSync is still overwritten. Closing that last gap needs a lock or an OS compare-and-swap, and this task rules both out. So the contract is DETECT-AND-RETRY, not absolute safety: any concurrent write observable at step 5 must be detected, the temp file removed, and the whole sequence retried from step 1. Mark the residual window with a ponytail comment naming the ceiling and naming a lockfile as the upgrade path if it ever bites.
- TEST: a concurrent rewrite of tasks.json landing before the step 5 re-hash is detected, does not clobber the other writer, and the archive is retried onto the new bytes and still lands.

---

description:
Split of task 130, step 3 of 4. Closes a task once its merge (task 151) has landed, then removes the worktree as the final step of the lap.

Run scripts/closeTasks.ts directly as plain code — no subagent. The close-tasks skill currently delegates this to an agent, which is why closure has drifted from what actually merged.

The gate is the merged commit hash, not control flow: closeTasks may only run after reading back the commit the merge produced and confirming the source branch points at it. "The pipeline reached this step" is not evidence — this repo has already shipped a blocked merge that archived its tasks anyway, and that is the exact regression this gate exists to prevent.

Record that verified hash in the archived record's commitHashes, so a closed task can always be traced to the commit that closed it.

THE COMPARE-AND-SWAP COVERS BOTH FILES, NOT JUST ONE. Closing moves a record OUT of .taskTools/tasks.json and INTO .taskTools/completedTasks.json. The read-hash-write-rename sequence must protect both, or the archive can be lost while tasks.json is protected. Order the writes so no state is reachable in which a task is absent from tasks.json and also absent from completedTasks.json: write completedTasks.json first, then remove from tasks.json. A crash between the two leaves the task in BOTH files, which is visible and repairable; the reverse order loses the record entirely. Apply the same hash-guarded rename to each file, with node:fs and node:crypto only — no new dependency.

WHAT THE HASH GUARD DOES AND DOES NOT PROMISE — narrowed 2026-08-09 by user decision, after codex rejected the first plan for promising more than the sequence can deliver. The guard is DETECT-AND-RETRY. It catches the realistic case: another writer changing the file while this one reads, parses and stages its write. It does NOT close the gap between the step 5 re-hash and the step 6 renameSync; a writer landing inside that window is still overwritten. Closing it would need a lockfile or an OS compare-and-swap, and this task forbids the lock, so the narrower contract is deliberate rather than an oversight. Do not plan, implement or review against the absolute guarantee. Mark the residual window in the code with a ponytail comment that names the ceiling and names a stale-timeout lockfile as the upgrade path.

WORKTREE REMOVAL BELONGS HERE, LAST. After the close succeeds — and only then — call removeWorktreeAndBranch to drop the worktree and the task-N branch. Find it by name in scripts/mergeTaskWorktrees.ts, which is in this task's files; do not cite it by line number, that file has drifted roughly 200 lines through this chain. Its position is fixed by plans/task-86-spec.md item 6: "run `scripts/closeTasks.ts` directly (no subagent), and `removeWorktreeAndBranch` **last**, so any earlier failure leaves the worktree for inspection." Task 151 deliberately does not make this call, precisely so that it lands after the verified close rather than before it.

MERGED BUT NOT CLOSED. If the merge SUCCEEDED but the close could not complete after its bounded retries, the merge is NOT unwound: the task stays open in tasks.json, the worktree is NOT removed, and the run reports MERGED BUT NOT CLOSED naming the merged commit hash. Task 149 owns emitting that outcome; this task owns producing it.

FAILURE OF THE FINAL REMOVAL IS NOT A FAILED TASK. If closeTasks succeeded and only removeWorktreeAndBranch failed, the task IS merged and IS closed. Report it as a cleanup warning naming the worktree path and branch, not as an unmerged or unclosed task, and do not unwind the merge or reopen the task. A leftover worktree is inspectable and removable by hand; a reopened task that already merged is not recoverable without a human untangling it.

A task whose merge was skipped or blocked is still present in tasks.json, not completedTasks.json, when the run ends. A concurrent rewrite of tasks.json that lands before the step 5 re-hash is detected, the temp file is discarded, and the retry re-applies the archive onto the other writer's bytes so neither change is lost. The narrower detect-and-retry contract is deliberate; do not test for safety across the re-hash-to-rename window. The workflow must supply the verified merge OID to closeTasks, not an arbitrary hash, and a skipped or blocked merge must never call closeTasks or removeWorktreeAndBranch at all.

title: tackle-tasks: on any lap-step failure nothing further lands, worktree survives, task stays open
userDescription:
## Goal

**Chain goal (tasks 150-153):** A task that clears the merge queue is completely finished — plan and brief deleted in the same commit, implementation notes committed, branches merged submodule-first, worktree removed, and the task archived against the verified merge commit hash — while a task that fails any step of its lap lands nothing further.

**This task is done when all of these are true:**

- "Failure" means failure of ANY step of that task's lap: the rebase, the per-layer tests, the conflict resolution, the fix loop, the cleanup, the merge, or the close.
- DEFINITION — "lands" means a SOURCE branch moved. Only a merge moves a source branch.
- DEFINITION — "nothing further lands" is measured, not described, and WHAT is measured depends on where the lap failed. For a failure BEFORE any merge (rebase, conflict, tests, fix loop, cleanup): `git rev-parse` of the PARENT's source branch returns exactly the hash it returned before that lap began, and no merge commit carrying this task's worktree changes appears on it. For a failure DURING the ordered merge: the parent is likewise unchanged, but submodule source branches that already merged stay merged. For a CLOSE failure after a successful parent merge: the parent legitimately DID move and must not be unwound — see the MERGED BUT NOT CLOSED bullet below. Never assert an unchanged parent hash for that last case.
- The conflict agent (task 145) and the fix agent (task 146) commit to `task-N` branches only. Those commits are not landings. They are not undone by a failure, and they survive on the task branch for the next lap.
- No submodule SOURCE branch is merged into after the point of failure.
- Submodule source branches that ALREADY merged before the failure are NOT rolled back (task 144). "Nothing further lands" bounds what moves next; it does not reverse what already moved.
- The task's worktree and branch survive intact for inspection — "intact" means still present and inspectable, NOT byte-identical to before the lap, since conflict and fix commits legitimately remain on the task branch.
- AFTER a successful parent merge, a close failure does NOT unwind the merge: the task stays open, the worktree stays, and the run reports MERGED BUT NOT CLOSED (task 152 produces it, task 149 emits it).
- The task is still present in tasks.json, not completedTasks.json.
- Two regressions this repo has already shipped make this the load-bearing part: a blocked merge that archived its tasks anyway, and a merge that left the source branch's index and working tree at the pre-merge base.
- TEST: one case per failing step, each asserting the point of the contract that step falls under. Rebase, conflict, suite and cleanup failures: the parent's source branch hash is unchanged from before the lap. A merge failure at a later layer: the parent is unchanged while already-merged submodule source branches are NOT rolled back. A close failure after a successful parent merge: the parent CARRIES the merge, the run reports MERGED BUT NOT CLOSED with that hash, and nothing is unwound. In every case the worktree and branch still exist and the task is still in tasks.json rather than completedTasks.json.

"Failure of what?" — failure of ANY step in that task's lap: the rebase, the conflict resolution, the full-suite run, the fix loop, the cleanup, the merge, or the close. "Lands" means a SOURCE branch moved; commits the conflict and fix agents make on `task-N` branches are not landings and are never undone.

The contract has THREE points in the lap and they are NOT the same rule:

1. BEFORE ANY MERGE — a failure in rebase, conflict resolution, testing or cleanup moves no source branch at any layer; the parent's source branch hash is exactly what it was before the lap began.
2. DURING THE ORDERED MERGE — submodule source branches that ALREADY merged before a later layer fails are NOT rolled back. "Nothing further lands" bounds what moves next; it does not reverse what already moved. The parent stays put until its own merge succeeds.
3. AFTER THE PARENT MERGE — a close failure does NOT unwind the merge. The task stays open, the worktree stays, and the run reports MERGED BUT NOT CLOSED.

In every case the worktree and its `task-N` branch still exist for inspection — "intact" means present and inspectable, not byte-identical — and the task is still in tasks.json rather than completedTasks.json. Two regressions this repo has already shipped make this the load-bearing part: a blocked merge that archived its tasks anyway, and a merge that left the source branch's index and working tree at the pre-merge base.

Scope of "failure": any step in that task's lap — the rebase (tasks 142-143), the per-layer tests and fix loop (146), the conflict resolution (145), the cleanup (150), the merge (151), or the close (152).

DEFINITION — "lands" means a SOURCE branch moved. Only a merge moves a source branch. Conflict-agent (145) and fix-agent (146) commits live on `task-N` branches, are NOT landings, are never undone, and survive on the task branch for the next lap. "The worktree survives intact" means it still exists and is inspectable — NOT that it is byte-identical to before the lap.

THE CONTRACT HAS THREE POINTS IN THE LAP, AND THEY ARE NOT THE SAME. Writing "the repository is exactly as it was" is wrong and unimplementable; write these instead:

1. BEFORE ANY MERGE — a failure in rebase, conflict resolution, testing or cleanup moves no source branch at any layer. `git rev-parse` of the parent's source branch returns exactly the hash it returned before the lap began.

2. DURING THE ORDERED MERGE — submodule source branches that ALREADY merged before a later layer fails are NOT rolled back. "Nothing further lands" bounds what moves next; it does not reverse what already moved. The parent's source branch remains unchanged until its own merge succeeds, so the parent never points at a commit reachable only from a task branch.

3. AFTER THE PARENT MERGE — a close failure does NOT unwind the merge. The task stays open in tasks.json, the worktree is not removed, and the run reports MERGED BUT NOT CLOSED (task 152 produces it, task 149 emits it). On the worktree point, the call ordering is already correct before this task starts: task 151 does not call removeWorktreeAndBranch at all, and task 152 places it last, after its verified close. So this task's job is the guard that keeps it from running on a failed lap — not relocating the call, not wrapping task 151's stage around it, and not adding a second copy of it.

title: addTaskFiles.ts must refresh run-arguments.json so the archive gate sees a widened fence
userDescription:
RETARGETED 2026-08-09, narrower than originally written. Read this whole field; the old scope is gone.

The original bug named skills/tackle-tasks/plan.workflow.js. That file is now dead code — nothing launches it. scripts/tackleTasksBrief.ts launches skills/tackle-tasks/task.workflow.js instead, and that workflow re-reads tasks.json fresh at the start of every stage, so the plan/verify/implement half of the original bug is already fixed and must NOT be re-fixed here.

What survives is smaller and still real. scripts/prepareTasks.ts snapshots each task's `files` array into .taskTools/run-arguments.json once per run. When a fence widens mid-run, scripts/addTaskFiles.ts appends the new paths to tasks.json, but nothing rewrites that snapshot. scripts/mergePipeline.ts then reads the stale snapshot at lines 85-87, where it uses task.files to verify the task's code actually landed before archiving it. A too-narrow list makes that archive gate check fewer files than the task really owns, so the gate is weaker than it advertises.

Observed live twice: on task 144, and again on task 153 on 2026-08-09, when the orchestrator widened a fence and had to re-run prepareTasks.ts by hand. That manual workaround should not be necessary.

Fix: after addTaskFiles.ts mutates tasks.json, it must also rewrite .taskTools/run-arguments.json so every task's `files` array there matches tasks.json. Reuse the existing resolveRunArgumentsPath helper in scripts/prepareTasks.ts rather than re-deriving the path. Update only the `files` arrays — do not re-snapshot the rest of the run, and do not touch mergePipeline.ts, which reads a fresh file once this lands.

description:

Up to six workflows may widen task ownership concurrently, but addTaskFiles performs unlocked whole-file read/modify/write operations on BOTH tasks.json and run-arguments.json (scripts/addTaskFiles.ts:41-51 and :64-76). runAsCli does an unlocked read / JSON.parse / mutate / writeFileSync on tasks.json, then a separate unlocked read-modify-write on run-arguments.json in refreshRunArgumentsSnapshot. AUTHORITATIVE-TARGET REQUIREMENT, settled with the user: the widening must land in the authoritative SOURCE tasks.json and run-arguments.json even when the planner runs inside its own private worktree. The audit flags this explicitly -- fixing C86-01 (task 166) by merely running inside the private worktree would introduce a second failure, because the private checkout has its own tasks.json while the authoritative source snapshot and source-created run-arguments.json would never receive the widening.

tests/addTaskFiles.test.ts today covers only single-writer behaviour, driving the CLI with execFileSync against a temporary .taskTools directory. It needs adversarial concurrent-writer coverage.

closeTasks reads tasks.json once and freezes the closing task record early (scripts/closeTasks.ts:85 and :103-113), building a `resolved` map keyed by taskNumber whose `task` field comes from that initial read. The completedTasks.json hashGuardedRewrite then archives each record as { ...task, completionDate, commitHashes, closureNote } using that STALE task (:115-129).

The closing plan's Edit 1.3 requires the two superseded instruction paragraphs to remain verbatim as //-prefixed text beneath a RETIRED marker. scripts/tackleTasksBrief.ts:164 currently contains only a one-line tombstone:

  // RETIRED (task 163): old close-tasks-skill text superseded by task 152's closeTasks.ts call; see git history.

That does not meet the task-86 spec's transitional rule, which says retired code stays commented out and only wholly superseded FILES are removed.

The expected pattern already exists in this codebase: scripts/runMergePhase.ts carries several `// RETIRED (task 147): ...` comments that retain the full superseded logic rather than pointing at git history. Follow that shape.

DIRECTION settled with the user: restore the commented text. Do not amend the spec -- the transitional rule stands, and changing it would loosen the rule for every other retirement in the codebase, not just this one spot.

THE EXACT TEXT TO RESTORE is recoverable from commit 6948357, which removed it from scripts/tackleTasksBrief.ts. The two paragraphs are:

1. "Close every task that is not problematic and was completed successfully, rendering its `tasks.json` entry stale, with **one** invocation of the `close-tasks` skill for all of them. Its first argument must be a JSON array of the task numbers with no spaces -- `[268,270,281]` -- followed by your reasoning for the `closureNote`s, naming each task (`#268 ...`, `#270 ...`) when the reasons differ."

2. "During implementation, you (the orchestrator) run typecheck only -- no test suites or visual checks. Workers run the tests covering the files they own and fix their own failures before reporting status complete; a worker with failing tests reports blocked or partial, never complete. Full verification (typecheck + full suite + the repo's UI verification where relevant) still runs once inside `close-tasks`, after the user approves closing."

Recover them from `git show 6948357 -- scripts/tackleTasksBrief.ts` rather than retyping, so they are byte-for-byte verbatim, and place them beneath the existing RETIRED marker, each line //-prefixed.

Watch out: tests pin the generated brief output byte-for-byte. These are comments in the emitter source, not brief output, so they must NOT change what the brief emits.
tests: Read scripts/tackleTasksBrief.ts, find the RETIRED (task 163) marker, and assert it is followed by the retired paragraphs as // comments rather than a bare tombstone line. It must fail loudly if someone deletes the body again.

title: Merge the plan and verify workflows into one pipelined step so each plan is verified as soon as it is written
userDescription: combine the planner workflow with the verifier workflow, so planning and verifying happen in the same step.  current behavior: a multiple-task planning session must finish before the multiple-task verify-plan session can begin.
description:
Root cause — two sequential barriers. skills/tackle-tasks/plan.workflow.js:74 is `const results = await parallel(TASKS.map((t) => () => runPlanner(t)))`, and skills/tackle-tasks/verify.workflow.js:97 is `const results = await parallel(PLANNED.map((p) => () => ...))`. `parallel()` is a barrier: it awaits every thunk before returning. Two of them in separate workflows, launched in order by skills/tackle-tasks/SKILL.md (Step 1 — plan, line 41; Step 2 — verify, line 45, which the skill explicitly waits on per lines 27-29), means no plan can be verified until the slowest plan in the whole run is finished. Wall-clock is sum-of-slowest-per-stage instead of slowest-single-chain.

Fix — the canonical `pipeline(items, stage1, stage2)` shape, which runs each item through both stages independently with no barrier between them, so task B's verify can start while task A is still planning.

Decision taken on file layout: create ONE new file, skills/tackle-tasks/plan-verify.workflow.js, containing both stages wired as a pipeline over TASKS, and delete both plan.workflow.js and verify.workflow.js. The user asked whether the two existing workflows could instead be run concurrently as-is; they cannot — each performs its own internal `parallel()` barrier over the full task list and returns only when complete, and SKILL.md awaits each in turn, so overlapping them would require rewriting both anyway. A single pipelined file is the smaller change.

What moves, verbatim unless noted:
- From plan.workflow.js: `PLAN_SCHEMA` (11-20), `testsInstruction` (22-24), `plannerBrief` (26-54), `runPlanner` (68-72) including its `PLAN_MODEL` override from ARGS.planModel (9, 70), and the null-result fallback record at 75-80 (`status: 'needs-clarification'`, `question: 'planner returned no result after 3 attempts'`).
- From verify.workflow.js: `VERIFY_SCHEMA` (11-21), `codexPrompt` (23-31), `verifierBrief` (33-84) with its codex → fable-medium → opus-4.8-high fallback chain (35-38) and the two-reviews-total cap (82), and the null-result fallback at 104-110 (`verdict: 'rejected'`, `reviewer: 'none'`).
- `retryAgent` is currently duplicated in both files (plan.workflow.js:60-66 and verify.workflow.js:89-95, byte-identical, each carrying the comment `// ponytail: null/undefined means the harness returned no result; re-spawn. Duplicated per file.`). The merge collapses two copies into one.

Simplifications the merge enables, which should be taken:
- verify.workflow.js:9 rebuilds `TASK_BY_NUMBER` from `ARGS.groups` purely to recover the task object that stage 1 already had in hand. In a pipeline the stage-2 callback receives `(prevResult, originalItem, index)`, so the task object arrives directly and that Map disappears.
- verify.workflow.js:112 `planFileFor` does `PLANNED.find((p) => p.task === task).planFile` with no guard — it would throw on a missing entry. In a pipeline the planFile flows straight through from stage 1's result; delete the lookup rather than porting it.

Behaviour that must be preserved exactly:
- Only `planned` plans get verified. `needs-clarification` and `not-relevant` plans must skip stage 2 entirely (short-circuit inside the stage-2 callback), not be sent to a verifier.
- The merged return must carry every key both workflows returned today, because downstream consumers read from both sets: `plans`, `planned`, `needsClarification`, `notRelevant` (plan.workflow.js:82-87) and `verified`, `approved`, `rejected`, `revisedCount`, `reviewHandoffs` (verify.workflow.js:116-122). `approved` entries must still be spread with their `planFile` attached (verify.workflow.js:118) because SKILL.md Step 3 passes `approved` straight to implement.workflow.js. SKILL.md Step 6 (lines 82-96) writes `needsClarification` and `reviewHandoffs` into run-steps.json, and both now originate from this one step.
- SKILL.md's Step 2 currently takes an added `planned` key in its args (line 47). That key disappears with the merge; the combined step takes only the pipeline args JSON as printed, like Step 1 does today (line 42).

**Test file that will break if missed:** tests/tackleTasksRetry.test.ts hardcodes `const WORKFLOW_NAMES = ["plan", "verify", "implement", "test", "merge"]` and `const EXPECTED_AGENT_CALLS = { plan: 1, verify: 1, implement: 1, test: 2, merge: 1 }`, then reads `skills/tackle-tasks/<name>.workflow.js` from disk. Deleting the two files makes it fail on a missing path. It must be updated to the new filename and its expected agent-call count adjusted for a file that now spawns two kinds of agent.

Ordering — open task #68 also edits skills/tackle-tasks/plan.workflow.js: it adds a `missingFiles` field to PLAN_SCHEMA and a re-plan retry loop around runPlanner. It must land first, or its edits target a file this task deletes. Soft interactions, not blockers: #58 edits both workflow files for the modifiableFiles/readOnlyFiles split (it has been rejected in plan review twice, so blocking on it would stall this indefinitely — let it rebase onto the merged file); and #75 copies the tackle-tasks SKILL.md body verbatim into a script, so #75 should land AFTER this task or it will faithfully copy the now-obsolete two-step wording.
tests: Return-shape only. Assert the merged workflow returns every key both old workflows returned — plans, planned, needsClarification, notRelevant, verified, approved, rejected, revisedCount, reviewHandoffs — and that a needs-clarification plan never reaches the verify stage. No timing assertions. Also assert each entry in `approved` still carries its `planFile`, since SKILL.md Step 3 hands that array straight to implement.workflow.js.
closureNote: superseded: v1.6 runs each task as its own independent block chain, so no cross-task plan or verify barrier exists

title: Assemble .taskTools/run-steps.json with a script instead of having the agent hand-Write it
userDescription: the run-*.json files should be generated programmatically, not via 'Update/Edit/Write'.
description:
Scope narrows to one of the three run artifacts. Two are already written by code: run-arguments.json at scripts/prepareTasks.ts:221-223 (mkdirSync + writeFileSync of the pipeline arguments), and run-outcomes.json at scripts/runMergePhase.ts:64-66 (writeFileSync of buildMergeOutcomes' result). The odd one out is run-steps.json — resolveStepOutputsPath, prepareTasks.ts:87-89 — which has no writer in the codebase at all.

Its only writer is the agent. skills/tackle-tasks/SKILL.md:79-99 (Step 6) instructs: "First, Write the earlier steps' return values verbatim to the stepOutputsFile path", shows a literal 7-key JSON skeleton, and then explains in prose (SKILL.md:93-96) which key comes from which step — done/partial/blocked/requeueCount from step 3, needsClarification from step 1, testReceipts from step 4, reviewHandoffs from step 2. That mapping being prose is the defect: the agent is transcribing four separate workflow return objects into one file by hand, once per run.

Blast radius of a mistake is silent and total. runMergePhase.ts:63 only checks that the file EXISTS; nothing validates its contents. buildMergeOutcomes (runMergePhase.ts:21-31) then coerces every absent key to 0 or [], so a dropped or misspelled key becomes a zero count rather than an error, and those counts plus testReceipts/reviewHandoffs are exactly what the approval gate and the merge command consume.

Shape of the fix: a script that receives the raw phase return values and derives the file, so the step-to-key mapping lives in code and the agent supplies only opaque payloads. Two hard constraints on how the payloads get there. First, workflow scripts cannot write the file themselves — the Workflow runtime gives them no filesystem or Node API access — so the values necessarily pass back through the orchestrating agent. Second, these payloads are large (full plan/verify/implement/test result objects), so prefer reading them on stdin over passing them as argv, which risks ARG_MAX truncation on a big multi-group run. The script should reject a payload missing a key it needs rather than writing a silently-zeroed file, closing the coercion hole above. SKILL.md Step 6 then loses the JSON skeleton and the prose key mapping, and gains a single command invocation.

Related but deliberately not blocking: task 86 restructures the pipeline into one workflow per group, which changes how these per-phase results are aggregated before they reach this file. Whichever lands first, the other adjusts the call site.
tests: Assembler round-trip test: feed the new script the four raw workflow return objects (plan, verify, implement, test) and assert the run-steps.json it writes parses to exactly the seven keys buildMergeOutcomes reads — done, partial, blocked, needsClarification, requeueCount, testReceipts, reviewHandoffs — with each value pulled from the correct step (done/partial/blocked/requeueCount from implement, needsClarification from plan, testReceipts from test, reviewHandoffs from verify), so a mapping regression fails the test. Add a case where one step's payload is missing a key the script needs and assert it errors out instead of writing a file that buildMergeOutcomes would silently coerce to a zero count.
closureNote: run-steps.json aggregation was retired by task 147; nothing left to fix

title: Name worktrees, branches and run files by task number so concurrent tackle-tasks sessions cannot collide
userDescription: it's possible for multiple sessions to use the same worktree group. find a way to ensure sessions never use the same worktree group when multiple sessions are active and running tackle-tasks simultaneously (maybe a lock file or job tracker file)
description:
**Root cause.** Every shared name in a run is derived from `groupId`, and `groupId` is just `index + 1` (scripts/taskGroups.ts:56), so it restarts at 1 on every run and carries zero cross-session uniqueness. scripts/prepareTasks.ts:134 builds the worktree path as `join(tmpdir(), "taskTools-wt", basename(repoRoot), \`group-${group.groupId}\`)` and prepareTasks.ts:95-97 builds the branch as `task-group-${groupId}`. Two sessions that start tackle-tasks on unrelated tasks both get group 1, therefore the same directory and the same branch.

**The collision is destructive, not merely shared.** createWorktreeForGroup (prepareTasks.ts:133-153) takes the `existsSync` path when the directory is already there and runs `git -C <worktree> checkout --force -B <branch> <currentBranch>` (:138-142). That force-resets the branch to the source-branch tip, discarding whatever the other live session had committed there. The comment on :137 shows the intent was reusing a worktree left by an EARLIER, finished run; it does not distinguish that from a run still in flight.

**Why groupId was chosen originally, and why the fix is still safe.** A group is not one task — TaskGroup carries `taskNumbers: number[]` (taskGroups.ts:8-13) because groupTasksByFileOverlap bundles tasks that share files and therefore must be implemented in one tree. groupId was the only single scalar a group had, and it arrived in the first commit that added the file (6b8fe68, "Step 3: add scripts/prepareTasks.ts"), never revisited for concurrency. But a stable per-group identifier already exists: members are sorted ascending (taskGroups.ts:50) and groups are sorted by their lowest member (taskGroups.ts:55), so `taskNumbers[0]` is deterministic for a given group.

**Decided with the user.** Name by task number, not by a lock: worktree `taskTools-wt/<repo>/<taskNum>` and the matching branch, using the group's lowest task number. This removes the collision by construction for sessions working different tasks, and as a bonus makes a re-run of the same task reuse its own worktree instead of whichever slot index it happened to land in.

**Residual case that must not be silently force-reset.** Two sessions running the SAME task number still resolve to one worktree. That is a genuine conflict — same task, same files. Replace the unconditional `checkout --force -B` with a check: reuse the worktree only when it is not owned by a live run, and otherwise fail with a clear error naming the conflicting task, rather than destroying commits. This is the only place a lock-like signal is needed, and it is far narrower than a general job tracker.

**Run artifacts collide the same way, and are in scope.** resolveRunArgumentsPath / resolveRunOutcomesPath / resolveStepOutputsPath (prepareTasks.ts:77-89) are three fixed paths under `.taskTools/`, written at prepareTasks.ts:221-223 and runMergePhase.ts:64-66 and deleted at mergePipeline.ts:238. Two concurrent runs in one repo overwrite each other's pipeline state. Open point for planning: a run spans SEVERAL groups, so a single group's task number cannot name it — pick one scheme and apply it consistently, either the run's lowest task number across all its groups or a per-run subdirectory such as `.taskTools/runs/<key>/`. The existing `runId` (prepareTasks.ts:68-70) is already carried in run-arguments.json and is available as that key if a task-number-derived name proves ambiguous.

**Blast radius.** Only two source files construct these names — scripts/prepareTasks.ts and scripts/mergeTaskWorktrees.ts — but the run-file paths are consumed by scripts/mergePipeline.ts and scripts/runMergePhase.ts, and a dozen test files hard-code `task-group-N` strings as fixtures. Cleanup must also be revisited: worktrees keyed by task number accumulate one directory per task rather than one per slot index, so stale ones need sweeping.
tests: Two-session collision test: prepare two runs over different task numbers against the same repo, back to back without cleanup in between, and assert they receive different worktree paths and different branch names, and that a commit made in the first run's worktree still exists after the second run has prepared — proving the second run no longer force-resets the first. Add a case where both runs claim the same task number and assert preparation errors with a message naming the conflicting task instead of running `checkout --force -B` and destroying the first run's commits. Add the equivalent assertion for the run artifacts: two concurrent runs must resolve to distinct run-arguments/run-outcomes/run-steps paths, so the second run's preparation does not overwrite the first run's pipeline state.
closureNote: worktrees and branches are named task-N in prepareTasks.ts, with a lease check instead of a forced checkout

title: merge stage must rebase the task branch on the target tip, run the suite, and merge only on green
userDescription: When a task has reached the merge stage, the merge workflow should 1) rebase the task branch onto the latest tip of the branch it will be merged into. 2) run the test suite. 3) merge only if all tests pass otherwise, fix tests until they all pass and then merge.
description:
**Confirmed by tracing the live --run call chain during the task 108 merge (run msjbgxlk-5mv1nlb66n7).** None of the three requested steps happen today.

**Step 1 (rebase) does not happen.** `runMergePipeline` in `scripts/mergePipeline.ts:92-248` never rebases a group branch onto the target tip. It records `baseOid` in the repository manifest at prepare time and later compare-and-swaps against it. When the target has advanced, that CAS fails and the run comes back `blocked` with a base-drift reason, handled by `confirmedBaseDrift` / `coordinateMergeRetry` in `scripts/runMergePhase.ts:134-184,205`. So drift is detected reactively and reported, never resolved by rebasing.

**Step 2 (run the suite) does not happen on a normal run.** The only place a test command is actually executed in this chain is `scripts/runMergePhase.ts:153`, `const testRun = deps.runScript(["sh", "-c", policyResult.policy.completeSuiteCommand], occurrencePath)`, and it is reached ONLY when `confirmedBaseDrift(initialVerdict)` is true at `runMergePhase.ts:205` - i.e. only on a base-drift retry. On a clean merge zero tests run. `scripts/mergePipeline.ts:144` merely reads the pre-supplied `input.testReceipts` and checks their `status` field.

**Why that matters beyond redundancy.** Those receipts come from the pre-merge worktree, so the tree that actually gets published was never tested as the combination it becomes. With one group it is harmless; with several groups consolidated together it is a real hole.

**Step 3 (gate on green) therefore reduces to trusting stale receipts.** The pass/fail rule is `judgeMergeRun` in `scripts/runMergePhase.ts`; approval readiness is `scripts/approvalReadiness.ts`. The fix-until-green loop already exists as `skills/tackle-tasks/test.workflow.js` (its `maxRounds` test-then-fix loop, default 3) - reuse it rather than writing a second one.

**Related defect found in the same trace, worth fixing here because it is the same lines.** The pipeline builds the consolidation commit with pure git plumbing - `git merge-tree --write-tree` then `git commit-tree` at `scripts/repositoryIntegration.ts:103-104` (whose header comment states it neither moves a branch nor touches a base ref) - and then moves the branch with a bare `git update-ref` in `publishCanonicalRef` at `scripts/basePublication.ts:60-65`. Nothing after `mergePipeline.ts:230` runs `git checkout`, `git reset`, or `git read-tree -u`. Result observed in practice on 2026-08-07: branch new-usage-graph advanced to commit 38dc596 containing the task 108 code while the working-tree copies of scripts/taskStats.ts and tests/taskStats.test.ts on disk were still the OLD versions - `git diff HEAD` showed 101 deletions. `git log` looked perfect; disk was stale. Nothing was lost, but the next edit to that stale file would silently revert the merge with no conflict. The `git checkout` calls that do exist (`mergeTaskWorktrees.ts:179,216`, `repositoryBranches.ts:77`, `operationBranches.ts:71`, `prepareTasks.ts:140`) all belong to the legacy `--merge` flow or to worktree setup and never execute in the `--run` chain.

**Constraint on the working-tree sync.** Do NOT use `git reset --hard` - the repo routinely has unrelated uncommitted work (tasks.json edits, plans/ files) that it would destroy. `git reset --keep <targetOid>` is the correct primitive: it updates index and working tree to the target but aborts rather than clobbering a local modification. The branch being republished is normally the currently checked-out branch of the canonical occurrence, so `git checkout` cannot be used for it.

**Suggested fix points, in preference order.** Rebase + suite run belong upstream of commit creation, in `runMergePipeline` (`scripts/mergePipeline.ts:92-248`) before `publishBases` at line 230, or in `coordinateMergeRetry` (`scripts/runMergePhase.ts:134-184`) generalized to run unconditionally instead of only on drift. The working-tree sync belongs immediately after the successful CAS in `publishCanonicalRef` (`scripts/basePublication.ts:59-77`) or right after `publicationResult.published` is confirmed at `scripts/mergePipeline.ts:230-231`.

**Test coverage note.** `tests/basePublication.test.ts` and `tests/runMergePhase.test.ts` exist. `tests/mergePipeline.test.ts` does NOT exist and will need to be created.
tests: Assert the merge is REFUSED when the complete suite fails on the rebased branch - no commit is created, no ref moves, and the reported status is blocked with the failure surfaced. Assert the merge PROCEEDS when the suite passes on the rebased branch. Assert a group branch whose base has advanced is rebased onto the current target tip before the suite runs, and that the suite runs against the rebased result rather than the original branch. Assert a branch already at the target tip skips the rebase but still runs the suite before merging. Assert a rebase conflict halts the run and reports the conflicting paths instead of merging anything. Assert that after a successful merge the checked-out working-tree files match the newly published commit - regression test for the observed case where branch new-usage-graph advanced to 38dc596 while scripts/taskStats.ts on disk stayed 101 lines behind. Assert the working-tree sync ABORTS rather than discarding unrelated uncommitted changes elsewhere in the repo (e.g. a modified tasks.json), proving reset --keep semantics and not reset --hard.
closureNote: v1.6 rebases onto the target branch, runs the full suite, and merges only on green

title: test_rebaseGroupOntoSourceReportsCleanupFailedWhenAbortFails passes under node but fails under bun
userDescription: Rewritten 2026-08-07 after the original framing was found wrong. Originally filed as a real pre-existing defect in rebaseGroupOntoSource, based on a bun test run. It is not a defect: the test PASSES under node --test, which is what package.json actually runs ("test": "node --test tests/**/*.test.ts"), and fails ONLY under bun test, where it reports status "conflicted" instead of "cleanup-failed". Verified both ways on the same tree. The real issue is a runner discrepancy, not a bug in the code under test. Decide whether that discrepancy is worth anything: either make the test runner-agnostic so bun and node agree, or document that bun is not a supported runner for this suite and move on. Low priority either way, since the repo does not test with bun.
description:
Verified on the merged tree at 7c28efbc48e2262b947beeb6a6d71c20837ea14c, running the same single file both ways:
- node --test tests/mergeTaskWorktrees.test.ts -> test_rebaseGroupOntoSourceReportsCleanupFailedWhenAbortFails PASSES.
- bun test tests/mergeTaskWorktrees.test.ts -> the same test FAILS at tests/mergeTaskWorktrees.test.ts:743 with actual "conflicted", expected "cleanup-failed"; 20 pass / 1 fail.
The full suite under node is 1165 pass / 0 fail, so node sees no problem anywhere.

The test shadows PATH so that the git invocation for `rebase --abort` cannot succeed, calls rebaseGroupOntoSource in scripts/mergeTaskWorktrees.ts, and expects the failed cleanup to outrank the plain conflict in the returned status. Under node that works. Under bun it does not, which points at bun resolving or spawning the git child process without honouring the shadowed PATH the same way node does -- so under bun the abort actually succeeds and "conflicted" is the honest answer. That makes this a test-harness portability issue, not a status-precedence bug in rebaseGroupOntoSource.

History worth keeping: this test was the sole failure that made a tackle-tasks run look red during task 112, and it cost a round of investigation before the runner difference was spotted. package.json defines node --test as the suite command; any future triage should run that before concluding a test is broken.

Scope decision for whoever picks this up: first confirm the mechanism by instrumenting which git binary each runner resolves. Then either (a) change the test to force the abort failure by a mechanism both runners honour -- for example injecting a failing command runner rather than shadowing PATH -- so the assertion holds under both, or (b) if bun support is not wanted, leave the code alone and record that bun is unsupported. Do not weaken the assertion: whichever route is taken, the abort-failure path must still be exercised under node.
tests: Under node --test, tests/mergeTaskWorktrees.test.ts test_rebaseGroupOntoSourceReportsCleanupFailedWhenAbortFails continues to pass and still exercises the abort-failure path. If the runner-agnostic route is taken, the same test also passes under bun test, with all 21 tests in the file green under both runners.
closureNote: bun test tests/mergeTaskWorktrees.test.ts passes 46 of 46 at bcc3b09; the false failure no longer reproduces

title: Drift test pinning the inlined blocker constants to scripts/blockerVerdicts.ts
userDescription: the inlined constants in skills/tackle-tasks/blockers.workflow.js  now duplicate scripts/blockerVerdicts.ts. If those two ever drift, the workflow breaks quietly. Create a test to ensure they don't drift.
description:
Three declarations are copied at skills/tackle-tasks/blockers.workflow.js:8-12 from scripts/blockerVerdicts.ts:5-13: BLOCKER_VERDICTS, BLOCKER_VERDICT_SCHEMA_FRAGMENT, and buildBlockerInvestigationPrompt. The marker comment at :7 states why the copy exists (workflow scripts run in a sandbox that forbids imports), so the duplication stays and the test pins it.

Use the mechanism already proven in tests/tackleTasksRetry.test.ts:14-24: locate the marker comment, slice the source region below it, compile that text with new Function returning the declared bindings, then assert against the real imports. Follow that file's convention of a negative-control test (:84-89, :104-107) proving the gate can fail.

Put the tests in tests/blockerVerdicts.test.ts, which already imports these constants, rather than a new file.

Second gap found while reading: WORKFLOW_NAMES at tests/tackleTasksRetry.test.ts:7 lists plan, verify, implement, test, merge — blockers.workflow.js is absent, so its retryAgent copy, its agent() wiring, and its sandbox-parse are all unchecked today. Adding "blockers" to that array and EXPECTED_AGENT_CALLS at :8 (value 1, one wrapped agent() call) extends three existing gates for two lines. Its retryAgent block already matches the others byte-for-byte, so the identical-helper assertion should pass unchanged.

title: Delete the local operations/<runId> ref once a run's push and archival succeed
userDescription: 'operations' branch names are unnecessarily long.
description:
Nothing in the codebase ever deletes an operations branch, so every run leaves one behind permanently. 34 have accumulated locally on branch task-86-chain.

**Where the ref is created.** `consolidateLogicalRepository` calls `moveRefFastForward` at scripts/runConsolidation.ts:154-155, which runs `git update-ref refs/heads/operations/<runId>/<slug>` in `canonicalRepoRoot`.

**Confirmed no deletion path exists.** Grepping scripts/ for `branch -D`, `branch -d`, `deleteBranch`, `update-ref -d`, `delete-ref`, `prune`, and `cleanup` turns up only `removeWorktreeAndBranch` (scripts/mergeTaskWorktrees.ts:431-434), which deletes the `task-<N>` worktree branch produced by `branchNameForGroup` (scripts/prepareTasks.ts:95-97). That is a different ref namespace and is not the right hook. `rewriteOperationBranches` (scripts/runMergePhase.ts:150-154) only rewrites the runId prefix in memory on retry; it never touches a ref.

**Where deletion belongs.** In `runMergePipeline` (scripts/mergePipeline.ts:140), after `pushOperationBranches` (scripts/mergePipeline.ts:266) returns and archival completes — `git update-ref -d <ref>` in `canonicalRepoRoot`.

**Must not run on an aborted run.** `RunConsolidationAbort` (scripts/runConsolidation.ts:44-51) carries a `preservedRefs` list precisely so a failed run keeps its refs for inspection. Deletion happens only on the success path.

**Note on push.** `pushLogicalRepository` returns `{kind: "skipped-unique"}` without pushing when a logical repository has exactly one occurrence (scripts/operationPush.ts:64-66). In that case no remote copy of the branch exists, so decide deliberately whether the local ref is still safe to delete; the converged commit is already reachable from the fast-forwarded occurrence branches returned as `fastForwardedOccurrenceBranches` (scripts/runConsolidation.ts:157-161).
tests: After a successful runMergePipeline, assert no ref matching refs/heads/operations/* remains in the canonical repo. After a run that aborts during consolidation, assert the operations ref is still present.

title: Shorten the operations branch name to operations/<runId>, dropping the redundant double-hashed repo slug
userDescription: 'operations' branch names are unnecessarily long.
description:
Live example of the name produced today: `operations/msk4o3lu-hxi0j7dze4b/parsed-github-com-matkatmusic-tasktools-572765a1-c8146a02`. 34 such refs exist locally on branch task-86-chain.

**What the branch is for.** It holds one run's converged result for one logical repository so it can be pushed to that repository's own origin — see `consolidateLogicalRepository` (scripts/runConsolidation.ts:117-170) and `pushLogicalRepository` (scripts/operationPush.ts:60-94). It is per-run x per-repo, which is why it is not named `task-<N>`.

**Defect 1 — the trailing hash is a double-sanitize bug.** `sanitizeSegment` (scripts/operationBranches.ts:44-47) appends an 8-char sha256 of its input. It is applied at scripts/mergePipeline.ts:115 to build `logicalGroup.logicalId`, then applied a SECOND time at scripts/mergePipeline.ts:249 to build `canonicalOccurrenceBranchName`, hashing the already-hashed string. `-c8146a02` is sha256 of `parsed-github-com-matkatmusic-tasktools-572765a1`.

**Defect 2 — the repo-identity segment is redundant.** `consolidateLogicalRepository` writes the ref via `moveRefFastForward` (scripts/runConsolidation.ts:155) into `canonicalRepoRoot`, which IS that logical repository's own clone. `operations/<runId>` is therefore already unique inside it; naming the repo you are standing in adds nothing.

**Decision made with the user:** drop the repo segment entirely. Target name `operations/<runId>`, ref `refs/heads/operations/<runId>`.

**Sites to change.**
- `buildOperationBranchRef` (scripts/runConsolidation.ts:108-110) stops taking `canonicalOccurrenceBranchName` and returns `refs/heads/operations/${runId}`.
- `canonicalOccurrenceBranchName` on `LogicalRepositoryConsolidationInput` (scripts/runConsolidation.ts:22) is COMMENTED OUT, along with its producer at scripts/mergePipeline.ts:249. Retired code in this repository is commented out under a `// RETIRED (task 165): ...` header, never deleted.
- `buildOperationPushOccurrences` (scripts/operationBranches.ts:89-102) returns `operations/${runId}` for every occurrence; its per-identity map becomes unnecessary.
- scripts/prepareTasks.ts:220 also calls `buildOperationPushOccurrences` and must keep agreeing with the push site by construction (this agreement was the whole point of task 111 — see plans/task-111-plan.md:223).

**Invariant that must survive.** Every occurrence of one logical repository must still receive the SAME `operationBranch` string: `pushLogicalRepository` pushes `canonical.operationBranch` (scripts/operationPush.ts:70) and `verifyOtherOccurrence` (scripts/operationPush.ts:43-58) fetches that same name from every other occurrence. `operations/<runId>` satisfies this trivially.

**Do not delete `identityKey`.** `identityKey` (scripts/operationBranches.ts:49-53) is still needed for logical grouping at scripts/mergePipeline.ts:115. Only its use as a branch-name source goes. `sanitizeSegment` may become unused by the naming path; check remaining callers, and if none are left comment it out under a `// RETIRED (task 165): ...` header rather than deleting it.

**Directory/file ref hazard — checked and cleared.** `operationBranchName` (scripts/operationBranches.ts:39-42) produces the sibling form `operations/<runId>/<occurrenceId>`, which git would refuse to coexist with a ref literally named `operations/<runId>` in the same repo. Its only caller, `setUpOperationBranches` (scripts/operationBranches.ts:76-87), has NO production caller — only tests/repositoryDiscovery.test.ts:292 and tests/operationBranches.test.ts, each operating in its own throwaway repo. Same finding independently recorded at plans/task-91-plan.md:17. Pre-existing stale refs all carry different runIds, so a new run cannot collide with them.

**Out of scope**, tracked separately as task 161: deleting the ref once a run finishes. Nothing deletes these refs today, which is why 34 have accumulated.

title: Add a .done file watcher so a waiting agent starts on its own
userDescription: use a '.done' file to signal when work is done, have another agent that is depending on that work monitor for that file, so that when the file lands, the waiting agent can begin their work without being instructed.  use a monitoring script that triggers when the file lands, and deletes the file after signaling that it landed.
goal: - Running the watcher against a path exits 0 within its timeout once a '.done' file appears at that path
- After the watcher signals, the '.done' file no longer exists on disk
- The dependent agent starts its work from the watcher's signal alone, with no human instruction
- If no '.done' file lands within the 24 hour timeout, the watcher exits non-zero and prints a clear message naming the path it watched, instead of hanging
- NOT in scope: wiring this handshake into skills/tackle-tasks/tackle-tasks.workflow.js or the blockedBy chain — a later follow-up task owns that
description:
Build a standalone done-file handshake as reusable scripts. Nothing in the repo does this today: a search of scripts/, skills/tackle-tasks/*.workflow.js, and tests/ for "monitor"/".done"/"waitFor"/"poll" returns no matches. Agent handoffs today are driven explicitly by the orchestrating workflow script, never by a watched filesystem event.

Add scripts/doneFileMonitor.ts: it watches for a sentinel '.done' file at a given path, signals the moment the file appears, then deletes the file so the next run starts clean. The waiting agent runs the watcher and begins its work when the watcher signals, with no human telling it to start.

The watcher takes a timeout of 24 hours. If the '.done' file never lands inside that window, the watcher exits non-zero with a clear message instead of hanging forever.

Out of scope for this task: wiring the handshake into skills/tackle-tasks/tackle-tasks.workflow.js or into the existing blockedBy chain. This task ships the standalone scripts only; a later task does the pipeline wiring.

Follows the repo scripts/ naming convention (mergePipeline.ts, occurrenceSync.ts). No existing file needs to change.
tests: An end-to-end test: spawn the watcher as a child process against a temp path, have a separate process write the '.done' file to that path, then assert the watcher fired exactly once, exited 0, and that the '.done' file is gone afterward. A second case asserts a short timeout produces a non-zero exit and a clear message.

title: Stop stagedDiffs.ts excluding tasks.json so a task-only change still produces a commit message
userDescription: the commit-message skill deliberately excludes tasks.json, so it will see an empty diff. So a task-only change produces no message at all, and there's no subagent to spawn because there's nothing to summarize. the empty-diff case above means any close-tasks or create-task run gets a blank commit message.  This causes the main agent to produce the diff message.  fix: update the skill to stop excluding tasks.json.  Blocked by the task to inject the diff directly into the subagents promt.
description:
The exclusion lives in exactly one place: `EXCLUDES` at scripts/stagedDiffs.ts:5, holding `:(exclude)*tasks.json`, `:(exclude)*completedTasks.json` and `:(exclude)plans/archived`. It is spread into both git invocations in that file — the diff itself at :8 and the `--raw -z` scan for moved submodule pointers at :12. Only the :8 use matters for this fix; the :12 use is a pathspec on a submodule-pointer scan, where task files are irrelevant either way, so unexcluding is harmless there.

The blank result is produced at stagedDiffs.ts:38, `if (diff.trim().length > 0)`, which suppresses the entire `=== repo ===` section when a repo's filtered diff is empty. A staging set consisting only of task files therefore yields zero bytes on stdout, and skills/commit-message/SKILL.md:10 — which instructs the agent to hand "the diffs above" to a Sonnet 5 subagent — has nothing to hand over. Confirmed by direct observation: several task-only sessions in a row produced no commit message at all.

History of the exclusion: it is inherited verbatim from the pre-skill era. The identical three-pathspec list appeared in skills/tackle-tasks/COMMIT_MESSAGES.md, which task 62 deleted when it converted that document into skills/commit-message/. The list was never re-justified for the skill; it was copied.

Decision and open point: remove `:(exclude)*tasks.json` only, as the user specified. `:(exclude)*completedTasks.json` is a judgment call the implementer should settle and state — completedTasks.json is 222KB and its diffs are proportionally large, but a close-tasks run stages BOTH files simultaneously, so leaving it excluded means such a run is summarised from the removal side alone. That is still a non-empty, summarisable diff, so it is not a blocker either way. `plans/archived` should stay excluded; that directory does not exist and the entry is inert.

Size is not a concern for tasks.json itself: the file is 134KB but a single create-task addition diffs to roughly 18 lines and a closure to a similar size, because the array is pretty-printed one field per line.
tests: In a throwaway git repo: stage a change to .taskTools/tasks.json and nothing else, run stagedDiffs.ts, and assert stdout is non-empty and names the tasks.json path — the case that produces a blank commit message today. Add a second case staging both tasks.json and completedTasks.json together, which is what a close-tasks run does, and assert the output is still not blank. Keep a negative case proving the change did not unexclude everything: stage a file under plans/archived alone and assert stdout is still empty.
